prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active peptide form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: Round 1 left one real question on B042, the third seat, and no one argued that the achievement should wait. The scientific case is unchanged and I weigh it on the merits rather than on the six first-place rankings: the incretin effect, proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1 in humans (Holst), the identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form (Mojsov), the receptor biology and the intestinotropic and metabolic actions (Drucker), then long-acting agonists with large randomised outcome data in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal disease. Originality, mechanistic clarity, independent confirmation and maturity are all very high. I keep the citation on physiology and the active peptide, and I would have it say in its wording that incretin-based therapy is the consequence, so the drug-development step is acknowledged without being credited as a name. A single-part prize also avoids the forced cuts that any pairing with B033 or B049 would impose on a three-person cap.
statement.case_against: The attribution is still the weak point and I cannot close it from the supplied record. Mojsov's priority relative to Habener and others is contested, and Habener is outside the credited names. Leaving out Knudsen means the prize does not name the person who led liraglutide and semaglutide, and a committee that reads the prize as tracking clinical transformation could fairly call the trio incomplete. If Mojsov's identification is shown to be equal or secondary to other work, my trio is open to challenge. The obesity indication also carries open questions on central mechanisms and long-term safety, which affect how broadly the citation should be worded.

responses.point: El-Manira holds that a complete arc from physiology to therapy needs Knudsen, and says he would swap Mojsov in only if the peptide-identification record proves firmer than he can verify.
responses.response: This is the one disagreement that matters, and I find his version coherent. We differ on what the citation honours. If it honours the transformation of patients' care, Knudsen is the stronger third name. If it honours discovery, which is where I place the weight, then identification and synthesis of the active peptide is a discovery-level step and the long-acting analogues are its development. His conditional offer is fair. My answer is that the supplied record gives no evidence that tips priority away from Mojsov, and nothing that tips it to Knudsen. Without that, I would not drop a name for the sake of a story with a complete arc. I keep Mojsov, and if the committee reopens it, his trio is a legitimate fallback and I would not call it a lesser prize.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius reads Holst and Drucker as the clear anchors, will not call Mojsov settled, and says the three names must be reopened if Habener's work proves equal or prior.
responses.response: I agree with the anchors and with her condition, and I want it stated openly in our discussion. The citation should read as physiology plus the active form of the peptide and should not imply that the priority history is closed. I also take her objection to my ranking in round 1: I put B027 above B033 because of clinical consequence, and I now think that was too generous. Nusinersen is a single-disease success on a platform that is younger than the other leading candidates, and B033 is a signalling principle confirmed for three decades. My answer is that B033 is the stronger alternative to B042 on scientific grounds, and I move it above B049 and B027 in my own thinking, though it stays an alternative and not a second part.

responses.point: Sandberg proposes B033 (Walter and Mori) as the cleanest fallback and prefers a two-person June and Sadelain version of B049.
responses.response: I agree that Walter and Mori is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and that is a real argument for B033 as a fallback if B042 cannot be allocated defensibly. I do not think we need to trade a B042 name for it, since three people already fill the cap and a two-part prize would cost Holst, Drucker or Mojsov a seat. On B049 I do not think a two-name version answers the problem, because Eshhar is outside the credited list under any subset, and dropping Rosenberg removes the person behind adoptive cell transfer. I would not take B049 up this year until that omission is settled, which is why I have moved it behind B033.

responses.point: Linnarsson holds that discovery credit sits with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov and that Knudsen is a major drug-development figure but not the third discoverer.
responses.response: I agree with the reasoning and want to qualify it as Sandberg did. Excluding Knudsen is a consequence of the three-person cap and of a discovery framing, not a judgement that drug development is of lesser worth, and I would want that understood. I disagree slightly with the idea that discovery credit settles Mojsov in. It supports her only if the identification of the active peptide is accepted as discovery, and that rests on a historical record that none of us has verified. I accept that risk, and it is why I say it is a judgement and not a finding.

uncertainties: Priority between Mojsov, Habener and others for identification of the active GLP-1 peptide cannot be verified from the supplied record.
Whether the committee frames B042 as discovery of physiology and the active peptide or as discovery plus development, which decides between Mojsov and Knudsen.
Long-term safety and central mechanisms for the obesity indication remain open and may bear on how widely the citation is worded.
If B042 is reopened, whether B033 with Walter and Mori is a better fallback than a changed B042 trio.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict applies to the preferred configuration. I disclose a Rockefeller postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard and about twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann; neither involves anyone credited for B042, B033 or B049. Deep brain stimulation (B012) and optogenetics (B045) are in my clinical and research neighbourhood and I would flag them if they came forward. As chair I add nothing beyond my own vote.
